page: Amazon Web Services x8aedz.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform features 96 dedicated physical cores running on AMD EPYC 9R05 processors with an x86_64 architecture clocked at 5.0 GHz. Built with a 1:1 core-to-thread allocation, it eliminates simultaneous multithreading overhead to provide dedicated per-core compute capacity. System memory measures 3072.0 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5, establishing a high density of 32.0 GB of RAM per core. Integrated local storage provides 7600 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, complemented by a 75 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance features no physical GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes show top-tier compute and memory throughput. The system achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 400,519.32 and a single-core score of 4,207.66. Geekbench testing returned scores of 3,083.0 in single-core and 30,116.0 in multi-core routines. Cache and memory subsystems demonstrated read bandwidths exceeding 1,058.63 GB/sec for uncached large blocks and 22,606.27 GB/sec for cached 16KB operations, with write throughput measured at 425.69 GB/sec. In memory operations, the server attained 330.98 million operations per second in Redis SET testing alongside a PassMark database score of 45,811.76.

The physical architecture is optimized for high memory capacity per core and large NVMe scratch volumes rather than graphical processing. While CPU-based LLM inference yields top-tier token throughput in prompt processing across 135M, 7B, and 70B models, token generation throughput remains limited compared to dedicated hardware accelerators. The absence of GPU units balances resource allocation strictly toward massive in-memory scale and high parallel instruction execution.

Given its massive memory footprint, high local NVMe throughput, and 96 dedicated physical cores, the x8aedz.24xlarge instance is suited for in-memory enterprise databases, massive caching deployments like Redis, large-scale data analytics, and high-throughput transactional database management systems.
